ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two concentric circles, and the gray part between the outer circle and the inner circle forms an annulus. On the left there is a vertical line segment AB, and its two endpoints A and B are on the outer circle, so AB is a chord of the outer circle; this vertical chord is exactly tangent to the left side of the inner circle. Reasoning: Let the common center of the two concentric circles be O, the radius of the outer circle be R, and the radius of the inner circle be r. Let the point of tangency of AB and the inner circle be M. Because a radius is perpendicular to a tangent line, OM is perpendicular to AB. Also because O is the center of the outer circle, the line passing through the center and perpendicular to chord AB will bisect that chord, so M is the midpoint of AB. It is known that AB = 32 cm, therefore AM = 16 cm. In right triangle OMA, OA = R, OM = r, AM = 16, so R^2 = r^2 + 16^2. Therefore R^2 - r^2 = 256. The area of the gray annulus is π(R^2 - r^2) = 256π. The area in the problem is kπ, so k = 256.

raw_record.question_text:
The diagram shows two concentric circles. Chord $AB$ of the larger circle is tangential to the smaller circle.
The length of $AB$ is $32\mathrm{~cm}$ and the area of the shaded region is $k\pi\mathrm{cm}^{2}$.
What is the value of $k$?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a gray annulus formed by two concentric circles, with vertical chord AB of the outer circle tangent to the inner circle on the left. Let O be the common center, R the outer radius, and r the inner radius. Let M be the tangency point of AB with the smaller circle; since OM is perpendicular to the tangent line and also perpendicular to the chord AB, M is the midpoint of chord AB. From the text, AB = 32 cm, so AM = 16 cm. In right triangle OMA, OA = R, OM = r, and AM = 16, so R^2 = r^2 + 16^2. Therefore R^2 - r^2 = 256. The shaded region is the annulus, with area π(R^2 - r^2) = 256π, so k = 256.
